# Plan: SPE round r01 for the triage agent

The repo has no `spe/` folder yet, so this is round r01. Date: 2026-10-21. Your spec is "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." That spec does not define "correctly" or "cheaply." I set defaults for both below and logged them as open decisions you own. You asked for local commits after each step. I will commit locally and never push.

Defaults I chose where details were missing:
- **Agent design:** The agent is one Claude Messages API call. It uses a forced tool call that returns `{category, priority, reply}`. It has no other tools in r01.
- **Stack:** Node.js with `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, because the Workflow script is JavaScript.
- **Data:** You give me the path to the 40 tickets and the support lead's labels. I convert them to `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl` and `spe/evals/data/labels.jsonl`. Historical tickets may hold customer data, so `spe/evals/data/` goes in `.gitignore`. Only a SHA-256 manifest of the data gets committed.

## 1. Specify

### Requirements (r01)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Assign exactly one category from billing, bug, how-to, account, outage | User: "triage tickets correctly" | `check_category_exact` against labels |
| R2 | Assign exactly one priority from P1 to P4 | User: "triage tickets correctly" | `check_priority_exact`, `check_priority_within1` |
| R3 | Never miss a P1 ticket | Decision D1 (default) | `check_p1_recall` |
| R4 | Draft a first reply that addresses the ticket, invents no facts, promises no refunds or fix dates, and asks for any missing info | Project description, decision D4 | `judge_reply_rubric` (blind judge) |
| R5 | Output always matches the schema | Decision (code needs it) | `check_schema` |
| R6 | Keep cost per ticket at or below $0.01, as long as category accuracy stays within 0.03 of the best config | User: "cheaply", decision D2 (default) | `meter_cost` from API usage fields |
| R7 | Do not tune prompts on the 40 eval tickets in r01 | Decision D3 (default) | Prompt files contain no eval ticket text. A grep check runs in the harness. |
| R8 | The eval data stays out of git | Decision D8 (default) | `.gitignore` entry. `git ls-files spe/evals/data` returns only the manifest. |

There are no proposals from an earlier round, because this is the first round.

### Open decisions (go to `spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Owner | Default for r01 |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Thresholds that count as "correct" | User | Category at least 0.90. Priority exact at least 0.75. P1 recall 1.00. |
| D2 | What "cheap" means | User | At most $0.01 per ticket at near-best accuracy (R6) |
| D3 | No held-out set exists. Tuning on all 40 would overfit. | User | No tuning in r01. Propose a 20 dev / 20 test split for r02. |
| D4 | No reference replies exist. Only labels exist. | User | A blind rubric judge grades replies |
| D5 | Exact model IDs | Claude | Current Sonnet and Haiku IDs, checked in the claude-api reference before the dry run |
| D6 | The priority rubric in C1 comes from general SaaS norms, not from the support lead | Support lead via user | I write it from the category definitions. It cites no eval ticket. |
| D7 | Where bug ends and outage begins | Support lead via user | Outage means many customers or a core service down. Bug means one feature broken for some users. |
| D8 | Whether ticket data may be committed | User | Not committed. Only the hash manifest goes into git. |

## 2. Predict

### Configurations (one change from C0 each)

| Config | Model | Prompt | Change from C0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| C0 | Sonnet | Category definitions with a short priority line | Baseline |
| C1 | Sonnet | C0 plus a written priority rubric with 8 synthetic examples (not taken from the eval set) | Adds the priority rubric |
| C2 | Haiku | Same prompt as C0 | Uses the cheaper model |

Each config runs 3 trials per ticket. That is 120 trials per config and 360 in total. A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. With 40 tickets, one ticket is 0.025 of accuracy. The bands are sized with that in mind.

### Numbers

| Metric | C0 | C1 | C2 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Schema valid rate | 1.00 ± 0.01 | 1.00 ± 0.01 | 0.99 ± 0.02 | `check_schema` | A forced tool call almost always returns valid JSON. Haiku may slip once on an enum. |
| Category accuracy | 0.85 ± 0.07 | 0.86 ± 0.07 | 0.80 ± 0.08 | `check_category_exact` | Most categories are clear. Billing versus account and bug versus outage will cause most misses. The rubric barely affects category. |
| Priority exact | 0.60 ± 0.10 | 0.70 ± 0.10 | 0.55 ± 0.10 | `check_priority_exact` | Priority follows the support lead's private policy. An explicit rubric closes part of that gap. |
| Priority within one level | 0.92 ± 0.05 | 0.95 ± 0.04 | 0.90 ± 0.06 | `check_priority_within1` | Models rarely miss priority by two or more levels |
| P1 recall | 0.80 ± 0.20 | 0.90 ± 0.15 | 0.75 ± 0.20 | `check_p1_recall` | The set likely has only 4 to 6 P1 tickets, so one miss moves recall a lot. The bands are wide for that reason. |
| Reply rubric pass rate | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.85 ± 0.08 | 0.75 ± 0.10 | `judge_reply_rubric` | Sonnet writes safe support replies. Haiku more often promises a fix date or skips a clarifying question. |
| Trial agreement (same label in all 3 trials) | 0.90 ± 0.06 | 0.92 ± 0.06 | 0.85 ± 0.08 | `check_trial_agreement` | Labels are mostly stable at the default temperature. Borderline tickets will flip. |
| Cost per ticket (USD) | 0.012 ± 0.004 | 0.015 ± 0.005 | 0.004 ± 0.0015 | `meter_cost` | About 2,100 input and 400 output tokens per call. C1 has a longer prompt. Haiku costs about one third as much. |

There is no earlier round, so `same_as_last_round` is null for every number.

The naive guess is a majority-class label for both category and priority. The harness computes it from the labels before launch. I predict that C0 beats the naive category accuracy by at least 0.40. I also predict that no config meets D1 in full in r01. C1 will probably miss "priority exact at least 0.75", and every config will probably miss "P1 recall 1.00".

## 3. Evaluate

### Steps and commits after you approve

1. **SPE r01 specify.** I create `spe/README.md`. I write `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md` with your prompt word for word. I write `spe/spec/spec.md` with the table above and `spe/spec/disagreements.md` with D1 to D8. I add `spe/evals/data/` to `.gitignore`. Commit: `SPE r01 specify`.
2. **SPE r01 predict.** I copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. I write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. Its first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It records round 1, date 2026-10-21, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs C0 to C2, each number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round: null`. Commit: `SPE r01 predict: C0-C2 baseline, rubric, Haiku`. This happens before any harness work.
3. **Agent build.** I write `triage/src/triage.js` and the prompts `triage/prompts/c0.md` and `triage/prompts/c1.md`. C2 reuses `c0.md`. Commit: `triage: r01 agent and prompt configs`.
4. **SPE r01 evaluate (harness).**
   - I write `spe/evals/harness/grade.js` with the code checks. I write `spe/evals/harness/judge-reply.md` as the judge rubric. The judge sees the ticket and the reply only. It never sees the config name or the model name. The judge uses a different model from the one under test (Opus).
   - I write `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js`. It sets `const ROUND = 1` once and builds every round label from it.
   - I write `spe/evals/data/manifest.sha256`.
   - Commit: `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)`.
5. **Gates before launch.** All three must pass or I halt and report.
   - **Grader selftest.** Grading the labels as answers scores 1.00. An empty output fails every check. A shifted copy of the labels fails `check_category_exact` on every ticket. One hand-written bad reply fails the judge.
   - **Control regrade.** There is no last round to regrade in r01. In its place, the harness grades the majority-class baseline and records it as the naive guess.
   - **Dry run.** 2 tickets x C0 and C2 x 1 trial. This confirms the schema, the cost metering, and the judge path. Dry run results are not counted.
6. **Launch the Workflow** with these arguments:
   ```
   { round: ROUND, configs: ["C0","C1","C2"], trials_per_ticket: 3,
     split_extra_trials: 2, split_cap_cells: 30,
     budget_usd_cap: 25, judge_model: "opus", dry_run: false }
   ```
   - Trials are plain API calls with no file or shell tools, so they cannot read graders, labels, or predictions. The harness still scans each transcript for tool calls and for label strings. Any trial that peeked is voided and logged.
   - Before each paid call, the harness checks the running spend. It skips any trial that would cross the $25 cap and logs the skip.
   - A ticket is a split cell when its 3 trials disagree. Split cells get up to 2 extra trials, for at most 30 cells.
   - The Workflow ends with a failure analysis that clusters misses into F-numbered types. A completeness critic then checks that every metric, config, and ticket has a result or a logged skip.
7. **SPE r01 evaluate (results).** When the completion notice arrives, I commit the raw results and the graded table. Commit: `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
8. **SPE r01 learn.** I write `spe/prediction-log.md` with Predicted, Measured, Verdict, and "Which Why broke". I say plainly if the naive guess beat a prediction. I write `spe/failures.md` with each F-numbered failure type. I add a "Proposed for round 2" table to the spec and write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`. I update `spe/README.md`. Commit: `SPE r01 learn`. Then I add the local tag `spe-r01`.

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

These figures use list prices from memory. I will confirm them in the claude-api reference before the dry run.

| Item | Calls | Est. per call | Est. total |
|---|---|---|---|
| C0 and C1 trials (Sonnet) | 240 | $0.012 to $0.015 | about $3.30 |
| C2 trials (Haiku) | 120 | $0.004 | about $0.50 |
| Reply judge (Opus) | 360 | $0.02 | about $7.20 |
| Split-cell extras and dry run | up to 70 | mixed | about $1.50 |
| **Total** | | | **about $12.50, hard cap $25** |

### Halt conditions

I halt and report to you if any of these happen:
- The budget cap is reached.
- Any sign shows that labels leaked to a trial.
- A grader gate fails.
- A result depends on D1, D2, or D7 in a way that only you or the support lead can settle.

I will not push, deploy, or send anything.
critiques: The plan quotes the user's prompt, "triage tickets correctly and cheaply", and maps it to requirements R1 to R8. Each requirement row has a Source and a Test column, for example R1 uses `check_category_exact` and R6 uses `meter_cost`. The undefined terms are logged as decisions D1 and D2.

The Numbers table gives C0, C1, and C2 specific values with bands for every metric, such as category accuracy 0.85 ± 0.07, 0.86 ± 0.07, and 0.80 ± 0.08. It also gives cost per ticket as 0.012, 0.015, and 0.004 USD. It uses no adjectives in place of numbers.

Every row of the Numbers table has a Why column with a concrete reason. One example is "About 2,100 input and 400 output tokens per call... Haiku costs about one third as much." The P1 recall row explains its wide bands by the small P1 count.

Step 2 copies the plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`, writes `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` with a do-not-edit header, and commits both. The plan says this "happens before any harness work". That puts the commit before the gates, the dry run, and the launch.

Step 5 lists gates that must pass before launch. They include a grader selftest (labels score 1.00, empty output fails, shifted labels fail, a bad reply fails the judge) and a dry run of 2 tickets x C0 and C2 x 1 trial. Step 6 launches the Workflow with explicit arguments.

The Numbers table has a Grader check column that ties each metric to a named check. Examples are `check_schema`, `check_priority_within1`, `check_p1_recall`, `judge_reply_rubric`, `check_trial_agreement`, and `meter_cost`.

Step 8 (SPE r01 learn) writes `spe/prediction-log.md` with Predicted, Measured, Verdict, and "Which Why broke" columns. It also writes `spe/failures.md`. It seeds the next round with a "Proposed for round 2" table and `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml`.
